falseFire.rule: THE FALSE-FIRE EXPOSURE — MODEL-FREE. Not a σ-band (a model is a prediction, and predictions are permanently rejected) but a HISTORICAL COUNT over the observable's own captured moat: 'a criterion at this level would have fired K times in the last N days of REAL captured data.' The exit evaluator, REPLAYED over the moat's own captures — the collapse-backtest, turned on the user's own criterion. Deterministic, reproducible, content-hashed, tiered REAL. NO distribution, NO σ, NO normality, NO prediction (PART A' attack #2: this corrects my own prior research recommendation and is a strict improvement).
falseFire.definition: FalseFire.count(criterion, series) replays ExitCriterion.evaluate over the observable's committed historical series (the defillama chart snapshot's dated points: tvlUsd/apyBase over time), COUNTING the points at which the criterion fired. It is a COUNT, never a model — a σ/probability/distribution ANYWHERE in the computation FAILS (S111).
falseFire.minHistoryWindow: DD-29 — the pinned minimum history is 180 days of captured points for the observable. Below it -> UNJUDGEABLE, and the fact SAYS SO (X-HONEST: missing stays missing). Above it -> the count is REAL (a count over content-hashed captures, not an estimate).
falseFire.rp2PointInTimeHonest: RP-2 (F-2, blocking) — a backtest has look-ahead bias. The count runs ONLY over point-in-time-honest captures and STATES which tier it used. The chart snapshot's points are each the value AT that ts (point-in-time by construction) and the snapshot is content-hashed (frozen); the count is reproducible over the frozen capture. If the series tier is REAL@ts (revisable) the count says so; a revised capture in the window -> the count computes on the unrevised subset and SAYS SO, or renders UNJUDGEABLE. Pin the rule before the code.
falseFire.renderSites: DD-30 — the DOOR (at exit registration, BEFORE the user commits to a threshold) and the DRAWER. It is a FACT so it travels in the Fact Envelope (authored:false) and it MUST pass the ONE GUARD. Speakable in both registers behind the five VoiceGates, no new intent.
falseFire.controls: S111 — a rendered ALTERNATIVE THRESHOLD FAILS (advice); a QUALITY SCORE/GRADE FAILS (verdict); a COMPARATIVE ('tighter than most') FAILS; a σ/distribution/probability in the computation FAILS (it is a count, not a model); deterministic x2; passes the ONE GUARD. The fact states the count and STOPS.

concentrationCeiling.rule: concentration-ceiling — THE FIFTH EXIT KIND. A SHARE IS NOT A VALUE. share = size / poolTvl is DIMENSIONLESS — no USD, no price, no oracle; the valuation ban is untouched. Answers the question the curator-loss literature is written about: a vault that had become the dominant supplier in a single market and could not exit — 'can I actually get out?'
concentrationCeiling.dd27SchemaHasSize: DD-27 — the tree showed the manifest Position ALREADY carries `size` (z.number().positive().finite(), the user's own units, NO USD conversion). So the fifth kind CAN evaluate for real users (F-4's 'no size field' prediction is WRONG — no schema change needed). RP-4: size does NOT enter the lineage content hash (a position's size changing is a rebalance, not a new hypothesis — hashing it would tag every rebalance as a SEARCH). Exit.concentration(position, poolTvl) is a pure helper; evaluate() reads a concentrationShare fact computed by the pipeline that holds both the size and the captured TVL.
concentrationCeiling.unitHonesty: share = size/poolTvl is a dimensionless ratio computed from two numbers the engine holds (the user's authored size, the captured poolTvl in USD). ORGANON does not price or convert; the ratio is a valid SHARE only if the user's size units match the pool's TVL denomination, which is stated. A seeded USD figure in the computation FAILS.
concentrationCeiling.controls: S112 — deterministic; UNJUDGEABLE without TVL or size (missing stays missing); a seeded USD figure FAILS; the exit set is CLOSED AT FIVE (a 6th kind without a pin FAILS); the combinator algebra is NOT built (its trigger pinned, not pulled).

pboTheory.rule: DD-25 / RP-7 (blocking) — the theory expectation is PINNED HERE, in Phase 0, BEFORE it is computed (X-DERIVE(f)). Under CSCV (Bailey/Borwein/Lopez de Prado/Zhu) on true-Sharpe-0 noise, the selected (IS-best) configuration should land below the OOS median about as often as above — by symmetry there is NO persistence in pure noise — so the asymptotic PBO is 0.5. V36 got 0.6 from BOTH implementations. If theory says 0.5 and both programs say 0.6, then two programs agree and both may be off, and that is a finding.
pboTheory.reasoning: asymptotic CSCV on i.i.d. true-Sharpe-0 returns: the IS-best strategy's OOS rank is uniform (no skill to persist), so P(below OOS median) = 0.5. Observed 0.6 is 0.1 above — outside a principled ±0.05 band. The temptation to widen the band or call theory UNJUDGEABLE is refused (RP-7); a pen that closes is a successful sprint.
pboTheory.d33Consequence: Signability.d33() computes SIGNABLE only when consistency AND theory AND non-shared-oracle all agree. Theory (0.5) vs observed (0.6) is a gap outside the band -> D33 recomputes to PRECONDITION-MET-BY-CONSISTENCY-ONLY. It went BACKWARD this sprint, and that is correct (D33 is fenced from K-activation).
pboTheory.nonSharedOracle: DD-25 (2) — a hand-rolled CSCV written DIRECTLY from the paper's algorithm, with its OWN Sharpe (a legitimate independent derivation, code we write from the method, not borrow). G-3: purgedcv's Sharpe is byte-identical to rigor._col_sharpe and PBO's delta was exactly 0.00e+0 — two 'independent' implementations producing bit-identical output on a combinatorial procedure is shared lineage, not independent confirmation.

delegatedDecisions.rule: Claude Code decides, documents, proceeds. A codebase-answerable question routed back to the Operator is a STALL. Each DD records the question, what the tree showed, the decision, the rationale, and the evidence as real output.
delegatedDecisions.DD25_pboTheoryAndNonSharedOracle: What does the published method predict for PBO on true-Sharpe-0 noise, and is there an oracle not sharing rigor's Sharpe? THEORY: asymptotic CSCV -> PBO 0.5 (no persistence in pure noise), pinned before compute (RP-7). NON-SHARED ORACLE: hand-roll CSCV from the paper with its own Sharpe. D33 SIGNABLE only on consistency AND theory AND non-shared-oracle; else PRECONDITION-MET-BY-CONSISTENCY-ONLY.
delegatedDecisions.DD26_publishedPredicate: What is the correct `published` predicate? `git branch -r --contains HEAD` is true on any clone. DECISION: publication means a STRANGER can get it — the narrowest predicate a local clone cannot satisfy: a release artifact at a public URL recorded in a committed release-manifest with its SHA-256, AND the remote is a known PUBLIC host (not a local file path). Proven false on the clone (S109).
delegatedDecisions.DD27_positionSize: Does the manifest position carry SIZE? THE TREE SHOWED: yes — Position.size (z.number().positive().finite(), user's units, no USD). concentration = size/poolTvl, dimensionless, no valuation. Size does NOT enter the lineage content hash (RP-4).
delegatedDecisions.DD28_mcpDependency: Does the MCP stdio server require a dependency? It must NOT. MCP over stdio is line-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 — the framing is WRITTEN directly (read stdin, parse, dispatch, write stdout); protocol version pinned; a malformed frame refuses not crashes. Dependency count stays 2 (hono+zod). @modelcontextprotocol/sdk on the mass path is a new mass-path dependency = permanently rejected.
delegatedDecisions.DD29_captureHistoryDepth: How far back does the moat's captured history go per observable? THE TREE SHOWED: the defillama chart snapshots carry dated point series (tvlUsd/apyBase), up to a 556-day span across 25 domains. Pinned minimum: 180 days of points for the observable; below -> UNJUDGEABLE; above -> REAL.
delegatedDecisions.DD30_falseFireRenderSites: Where does the false-fire fact render? The DOOR (at exit registration, before commit) and the DRAWER; it travels in the Fact Envelope (authored:false) and passes the ONE GUARD; speakable in both registers, no new intent.
delegatedDecisions.DD31_verifyThirdSubCheck: verify's third sub-check — restore or retire? DECISION: RESTORE (the curated-subset count vs committed IS a meaningful invariant — do_verify checks it). D54; the sub-check set declared and stable (S114). Silence forbidden (X-DEVLEDGER).
delegatedDecisions.DD32_commitBuildLogs: Where do the build logs get committed, and does it break anything? Under record/, hash-chained, explicitly NOT a source of truth for any producer (a wall asserts no Claim.producer reads a build log — X-DERIVE reads artifacts). Then every new wall names its originating defect in the pins at mint time (S108).
